A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CreatiLayout and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation and layout-planning experiments, quantitative benchmark results, and network and training ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds FLUX, LoRA, computational-overhead, and user-study results.

M1.justification: v2 adds SiamLayout-FLUX, adapting layout integration to FLUX's double-stream and single-stream blocks, and SiamLayout-LoRA, introducing low-rank updates to frozen linear and MLP layers. These extend the image-generation architecture beyond v1's SD3 implementation; the LoRA adaptation of LayoutDesigner already existed in v1.

E1.justification: Both use LayoutSAM/LayoutSAM-Eval, COCO 2017, T2I-CompBench, and the same caption-, center-point-, and suboptimal-layout planning tasks. The additional model variants, efficiency measurements, and human ratings do not establish additional datasets or distinct task scenarios.

E2.justification: HiCo is added to the LayoutSAM-Eval comparison in Table 2 and participates in the new efficiency comparison and user study. The earlier comparators remain in their corresponding benchmark tables; Reason Out Your Layout is only cited, not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds FLUX.1-dev and LoRA configurations, a user study using 100 randomly sampled examples and nine criteria, and relative MAC measurements for one denoising step with ten entities. Section 4.1 also adds IR and Pick to the stated COCO metrics, although Table 3 provides neither score. Existing dataset splits and stated training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C and Table 7 add a focused analysis of layout-control accuracy versus additional parameters and computation, including the LoRA alternative. The original network ablations, training-strategy analysis, and modality-competition analysis remain unchanged, including material moved from v1 Appendix B to v2 Appendix F.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new user-study win rates are point results without uncertainty estimates; sampling 100 examples changes the evaluation design.

E6.justification: Existing SD3 benchmark scores are retained. Table 2 adds HiCo and FLUX results, including FLUX spatial accuracy 95.67 and FID 16.12 under the new backbone configuration. Table 7 adds LoRA accuracy and overhead results, and Figure 11 adds user-study win rates. Table 2 retains the old FID improvement of +0.57, inconsistent with the new best FID of 16.12 versus the best baseline's 19.67, a difference of 3.55.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention equations, and training objectives in Equations 1–12 are retained. The new variants are described architecturally without new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: SiamLayout, LayoutSAM and its evaluation benchmark, and LayoutDesigner. Claims about precise generation and complex-attribute control remain substantively unchanged; the additional experiments support the existing broad MM-DiT positioning.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions interpret FLUX results as evidence of applicability across MM-DiTs and explain the parameter/control tradeoff of SiamLayout-LoRA. The efficiency discussion links InstanceDiff and HiCo computation to per-entity attention. Existing limitations concerning planner cost and annotation noise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 identifies FLUX.1-dev and specifies the image-generation LoRA rank as 256 and its adapted layers. v1's standalone 1.28B additional-parameter statement is removed, while Table 7 supplies relative parameter and MAC overheads. Other training details are retained, and the same project link is relocated to the first page.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Reason Out Your Layout and HiCo, bringing HiCo into the empirical comparisons. The broader related-work organization and positioning against UNet-based layout-generation methods remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. v2 adds FLUX/LoRA cross-references, distinguishes SiamLayout-SD3 in labels, edits the author and affiliation block, and places four new appendix sections before the existing material, renumbered from A–C to E–G.

P2.justification: v2 adds two architecture diagrams, a user-study chart, and an efficiency table. Table 2 gains rows and three-level ranking emphasis, while Figure 5 gains a FLUX output column. Existing displays are rearranged, including the retained supplementary Figures 9–13 becoming Figures 12–16.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence for portability beyond SD3 and makes parameter/computation tradeoffs assessable through the FLUX and LoRA additions and Table 7, while preserving the original experiments. These provide a useful net improvement, tempered by the user study's missing rater count and uncertainty reporting and Table 2's stale FID improvement summary.
